## 9de65c6eed00

**Reproduced authority/description disagreement, outside the documented generator domain.** The task prose/title describes subtracting the smallest object from the largest. The canonical Racket authority sorts objects by size and uses the first two, so on a three-object input with sizes `5,3,1` it subtracts the **second-largest** (size 3), not the smallest (size 1).

The exact input is `checks/audit/9de65c6eed00/input.json`. The supported Racket apply run executed rule hash `5c7d71fc1b03`; its output differs from the written-solution rival in `checks/audit/9de65c6eed00/audit.json`, with full source/input/output hashes in `checks/audit/9de65c6eed00/racket.json`. The selected generator hash was `b88575156cdbd3881203d72d387ad19d70842695b2fd99bf71239044e9cd733f`.

This input does **not** pass the target validator: `self_check` reports `expected exactly two connected objects, found 3`, and the default generator emits exactly two objects. Therefore this is not a counterexample to generated lessons; it is a latent disagreement between the general authority and the natural-language “smallest” description that the generator's narrow domain masks. No audit-target file was changed.

Reproduction command from the packet root:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 9de65c6eed00 \
  --input ../checks/audit/9de65c6eed00/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/9de65c6eed00/racket.json
```
